speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chair, at the heart of the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF's) work is our firm conviction that strong families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We strive to make Singapore the best place for all families to grow and flourish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, I will share four areas where MSF supports families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, how we are journeying with families through every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, how we are uplifting families with caregiving needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And fourth, how we are fostering a family-friendly Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, around nine in 10 Singaporean children aged three to six are enrolled in preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have enhanced access to affordable and quality preschools, by ramping up the number of preschool places available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In particular, we increased the number of Government-supported preschool places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is, we are on target and we will be able to provide places for 80% of preschoolers in a Government-supported preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It gives me great satisfaction to say this, because together with fellow women Members of Parliament (MPs), like Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Joan Pereira, together, we had put up a proposal in 2019 then, to the Government to increase the number of Government-supported preschool places and to lower costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, the Government has been working hard over the years, and I am glad to share that now, in my position as the Minister of State at MSF, we have managed to see these proposals through.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And now, 80% of our preschool children can go to Government-supported preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government will not stop at this achievement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about the affordability of preschool services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government provides all Singaporean children with basic subsidies of up to $300 each for full-day childcare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also additional financial subsidies for eligible families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2020, we raised the household income ceiling so that more families can qualify for means-tested additional subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also enhanced subsidy amounts across all eligible income tiers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Eligible families can now receive means-tested additional subsidies, which range from $80 to $467 for full-day childcare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, we have been steadily reducing full-day childcare fee caps for AOP and Partner Operators (POP), with a reduction of $40 for monthly fees in 2023, another reduction of $40 at the start of this year in 2025 and an additional $30 reduction in 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Compare this to $720 for AOP in 2021 and $760 for POP in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With these fee reductions, we will meet another commitment that this Government made in 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is, that full-day childcare expenses before means-tested subsidies will be similar to what households pay for primary school and after-school care fees combined.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Melvin Yong asked about further quality improvements in our preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With effect from 2025, the Singapore Preschool Accreditation Framework (SPARK) 2.0 supports preschools to further improve their quality and be appraised against higher standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The new Quality Teaching Tool will also be rolled out in 2025 to guide and hone educators' pedagogical skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Attracting and retaining good educators is a priority for us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA engaged with preschool teachers, centre leaders and operators, and this led to initiatives to improve retention, such as Saturday closure, designating Teachers' Day and Children's Day as preschool holidays and designating six development days for educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also embarked on an educator-centric review of their teaching experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Deepening our understanding of their motivations and challenges will help us do even more to enhance the attraction, retention and experiences of early childhood educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continually review our programmes and initiatives, and work with the sector so that our children can benefit from high-quality early childhood care and education; and parents are assured of high teaching standards; and our educators are motivated and equipped to do well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also strengthened support for children with developmental needs by increasing the number of Government-funded places for children requiring medium- to high-levels of early intervention support by almost 80% since 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC)-Care pilot, introduced in 2024, also equips caregivers with skills to support their child's development at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we are doing more to journey with families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Families for Life (FFL) Movement, led by the FFL Council, brings together partners and volunteers to promote a family-friendly society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Couples preparing for marriage, or already-married couples can participate in FFL's marriage preparation and enrichment programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim that educators and parents play an important role in building a family-friendly Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nurturing a positive parent-preschool partnership is a key focus area in ECDA's refreshed "Shape Our Tomorrow" campaign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under FFL@Community, families can conveniently access programmes and peer support groups to equip them with the skills and confidence to care for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many corporates have stepped forward to partner the FFL Council in supporting families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some have organised FFL parenting talks; others have arranged family days for staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many employers also support their employees with caregiving needs by adopting flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope more employers can join us to foster a family-friendly workplace culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year's Family trends report showed greater marriage stability in recent cohorts, with falling rates of marriage dissolution before the 10th anniversary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In a 2023 MSF survey on families, 86% of families reported moderate to high family resilience scores, meaning that they were generally able to recover from challenges together, and the majority of respondents also reported having close-knit families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gerald Giam had asked about support for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We appreciate our caregivers for the pivotal roles that they play in the care for their loved ones, the sacrifices they make, and we want to support them in their care for their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Prime Minister mentioned in his Budget round-up speech, it is difficult to put a monetary value on the love and care that caregivers provide for their loved ones, and we also should not think of family relationships in terms of monetary value.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It would be a sad day for family relationships if we need to be paid so that we will be willing to take care of our aged parents, our children or grandparents taking care of their grandchildren.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But that said, to support caregivers, the Government provides help to defray the cost of taking care of the loved ones in the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, this comes through the form of the enhanced Home Caregiving Grant, which the Government has been increasing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It has been increased for the second time in two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To recap, the Home Caregiving Grant was introduced in 2019 to improve affordability for long-term care and to support caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I know this because I spoke to caregivers during the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development in 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I spoke to caregivers and asked how we can support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, we have been listening to caregivers and we want to support them when they care for their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This approach, through the Home Caregiving Grant, also takes into account the fact that caregiving arrangements can vary from family to family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Besides the Home Caregiving Grant, the Government also multiplies the support that families provide to their caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) and the newly announced five-year Matched MediSave Scheme enables families and loved ones to contribute to the retirement and healthcare needs of lower-income seniors, including caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Help for caregivers also come in the form of the Caregivers Training Grant to attend approved courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Partners, such as CaringSG, also empower caregivers through initiatives which bring peer- and community-based supports closer to home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For caregivers of children, apart from the decade-long push for more accessible, more affordable and quality preschools which I had touched on earlier, we have also announced a new pilot to help parents with infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents with infants can tap on infant care centres or the three-year childminding pilot which was launched last December.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This month, we launched childminding services from Tampines East Community Club, with services from Nee Soon East Community Club expected to start later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana asked about support for fathers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have doubled the Government-Paid Paternity Leave scheme and enhanced employment protection for fathers on paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FFL also partners the Centre for Fathering to promote active fathering through programmes and peer support groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Children come from a diverse range of family backgrounds, such as single-parent families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng has been advocating for single unwed mothers for several years now.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The cash component of the Baby Bonus is given to married couples to support them as they start a new family together and that is why it is called a "Baby Bonus Cash Gift".

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And for couples and families facing stressors in their marital or family relationships, they can tap on the Strengthening Families Programme at Family Service Centres (FAM@FSC), for support services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families in need of financial assistance may also approach Social Service Offices or Family Service Centres for holistic case management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are doing more to support parents with the costs of child-raising.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We empathise with couples who want more children but are concerned about child-raising costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All parents are also supported through the Child Development Account (CDA), where parents receive the First Step Grant and Government co-matching for deposits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: CDA funds can be used at Baby Bonus Approved Institutions for specific expenses that directly benefit the child, such as preschool uniforms and field trips organised by preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We had sought feedback from parents on the CDA's approved uses to ensure it remains useful for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most parents feel that the existing coverage is sufficient, but some were keen on using the CDA for other preschool incidental costs which are currently not included, such as enrichment classes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some families said that they tended to opt out of such optional programmes as they could not afford it and they were unable to tap on the CDA for such activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will thus be expanding the use of the CDA scheme to better meet families' needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This would cover enrichment programmes provided by the preschools, such as speech, drama, robotics and coding classes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, for many, the expansion of the CDA uses will provide more financial support for their preschoolers to fully tap on the learning opportunities offered by their preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I would now like to touch on parents with children with special needs or persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In my work at the Ministry of Education (MOE), I have met several parents who have children with special needs, and even in my work at MSF, I have met with parents who have young children with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Often times, they share their deepest worry, which is who is there to take care of their child after they are gone?

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Most parents worry about their children as they grow older, the children grow up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But for parents with children with special needs, that worry is even more acute because they worry about how their child will be able to live independently after they are gone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, this time round, the Government will be embarking on two initiatives to help parents with children with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) had announced, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme will be expanded to persons with disabilities of all ages to help them build up sufficient retirement savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This increases their retirement savings and monthly payouts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If a parent of a seven-year-old child diagnosed with autism makes a cash top-up of $2,000 annually for 10 years, their child will see an increase in CPF retirement savings of at least $320,000 when he is 65 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will allow the child to receive an increase of $1,700 in monthly payouts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF will also enable more families of persons with disabilities to plan early for the financial security of their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) works with parents of children with disabilities to prepare a detailed care plan that sets out how their children will be cared for after they have passed on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The developed care plan will determine how much money is needed for their child and how that sum can be built up in the trust account, such as through cash, property, CPF savings and insurance payouts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: After the caregivers pass on, SNTC will disburse the monies in the Trust account according to the care plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF will subsidise SNTC's fees for Trust services to keep this affordable for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, for a family with a seven-year-old child diagnosed with autism, if the parents top up the SNTC trust account with $10,000, the Government will match this, bringing the total amount in the trust account up to $20,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They can then use this sum to defray the insurance premium for a term plan of at least $100,000, in a sum assured in their name, and this builds up financial security for the child, as the sum assured will go into the trust account when the caregiver passes on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope that parents of persons with disabilities will feel more reassured that their child will be supported, even though they may no longer be around to do so themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: My colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, will share more about MSF's other moves to build an inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Lastly, beyond enhanced financial and caregiving support, we are celebrating families as a nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Designating 2022 as the Year of Celebrating SG Families underscored the importance of our families, and National Family Week has also grown into the National Family Festival, which attracted more than 700,000 participants in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about our plans to foster a family-friendly Singapore, and one way we have done so is by expanding family-oriented spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2022, we unveiled Family Zone at Gardens by the Bay for all families to enjoy quality time together and celebrate key life milestones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This represents MSF's commitment, alongside our partners, to create shared spaces for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This year, with the strong support from MSF's partners, we will be introducing new features to the Family Zone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our children can learn shared family values through play at the new family playground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Children of different abilities can also come together and enjoy the inclusive play equipment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also launch the enhanced community garden, which can host visits and workshops for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This garden will be tended to by volunteers, many of whom are seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Family Zone was made possible through our collaboration with partners from the people and private sector, namely, Gardens by the Bay, PropNex and the Community Chest (ComChest).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We invite more corporate partners to come on board to offer meaningful experiences for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairperson, if I may speak in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government has been working hard through various policies and measures to help every Singaporean family grow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We know that young parents in Singapore are very concerned about the cost of raising a child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Therefore, we have been committed to providing more quality and affordable preschool centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also been reducing full-day childcare fee caps for anchor operators and partner operators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through these fee cap reduction measures, we will keep full-day childcare expenses affordable, comparable to primary school fees plus after-school care fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For families that have children with special needs, we also have a series of support measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Additionally, we have the Special Needs Trust Company scheme, where parents can top-up funds to the Special Needs Trust Company account of their special needs child, and the Government will provide a matching grant of up to $10,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If the parents and caregivers are no longer around, SNTC will care for these special needs children according to the care plan. : Mr Chairman, this SG60, as we look back at how far we have come, I hope that we are also excited of the road ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, we can do even more to create a Singapore where every child has a good start in life and where every family has the opportunity to thrive and to flourish.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As we look ahead, it is important to consider what society we want to be.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A lasting goal for Singapore is to remain a place of opportunities and hope.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many Singaporeans want Singapore to continue to be a place where all families thrive, including lower-income and vulnerable families, and those with family members with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF is committed to supporting these families and today, I will share the progress we have made and our way forward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We remain committed to journeying with lower-income families towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We started with providing a strong safety net to support those who need help with basic needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is the philosophy behind ComCare financial assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While families are our first line of support, some may require additional help from the Government and the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over the years, we have enhanced ComCare to reflect the evolving cost and definition of basic needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To Ms Ng Ling Ling's query, ComCare caters for a range of food options so that families can buy food items they prefer without compromising on nutrition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This ensures they need not cut back on food expenditure at the expense of their health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With ComCare support, families can stabilise their footing and can better pursue longer-term goals of self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, social assistance alone addresses immediate needs but may not tackle the underlying causes of challenges or provide longer-term solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Moreover, those in need may not have the time or capacity to reach out for support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under ComLink+, we go beyond assistance, to empower families to achieve their goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We proactively reach out to lower-income families and address their needs early.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family coaches journey with them by co-creating action plans tailored to their strengths, needs and goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through the ComLink+ Progress Packages, we boost their efforts, providing financial top-ups to those that take action in preschool enrolment and attendance, employment, debt clearance and home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It has also been expanded to lower-income families not in public rental housing, but are eligible for the KidSTART programme or have school-going children at risk of long-term absenteeism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The ComLink+ Progress Packages for Preschool and Employment were launched in August and December 2024 respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The ComLink+ Packages for Debt Clearance and Home Ownership will be launched in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each family coach works with 25 to 35 families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Riyaz, his wife and their four-year-old daughter, Inayah, live in a 2-room rental flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A full-time cook, Mr Riyaz is the sole breadwinner while his wife cares for their daughter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Their family coach, Ms Hazriah, built on their aspirations and strengths and marshalled resources to support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Tapping on the couple's focus on Inayah's education, she emplaced them on the ComLink+ Package for Preschool to incentivise good attendance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: She also collaborated with KidSTART in providing and supporting Inayah's child development needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Riyaz and his wife also hope to find well-paying employment to provide a better life for Inayah.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Recognising this, Ms Hazriah emplaced him on the ComLink+ Package for Employment and referred his wife to basic English courses to improve her employment prospects.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is but only one example of how ComLink+ recognises families' strengths, efforts and aspirations and empowers them towards their goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Fahmi Aliman and Mr Melvin Yong will be pleased to know that we will be further integrating services across Government to deliver even more comprehensive, coordinated and convenient support to uplift lower-income families under ComLink+.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, we are weaving health and social support together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Being healthy allows us to live, work and pursue our aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But families trying to make ends meet may find it hard to keep track of medical appointments or need help identifying relevant healthcare services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family coaches will support families in adopting healthier lifestyles through healthier diet, exercise and regular health screenings, among other measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Dedicated staff from healthcare clusters will help families access services that they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And for families with complex health conditions, family coaches and healthcare staff will help develop and implement health action plans that prioritise their needs, steps to take and healthcare services to access.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through this, we hope to improve families' overall health, such that they can better pursue their other life goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will use insights from the trial to support more families in due course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many ComLink+ families in public rental housing aspire to own a home and we are enhancing our support to enable their aspirations in two ways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim shared, from entry to public rental housing, HDB officers support ComLink+ families in working out the income and savings they need for homeownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family coaches will journey with them towards these goals and when they are ready to purchase a flat, HDB will help them navigate the process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, we are opening more pathways homeownership through enhancing the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this, more families can realise their homeownership aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chair, we have significantly pivoted our support for lower-income families, moving from assistance to empowerment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to invest our efforts in this area so that families in need can achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Familial support networks may shrink and weaken over time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With our ageing population, we will see an increase of senior households, social isolation and caregiving stress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The proportion of dual-income families has also grown and more face challenges balancing family commitments and career demands.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Domestic violence continues to be an issue faced by some families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have already seen an increase in the volume and complexity of family service cases social service professionals deal with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To prepare well for the future, we must grab the bull by its horns, tackle the challenges early and head-on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But to be sure, it is not all doom and gloom.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, the social service sector is in a position of strength, having grown in professionalism and recognition over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, Mr Louis Ng would be happy to know that we are stepping up efforts to manage the heavy demands placed on social service professionals today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Imposing a strict cap on caseloads would be unnecessarily rigid, as the sector needs flexibility in manpower deployment to adapt effectively to operational needs on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are focusing on other areas and ways to manage the demand, by expanding the sector workforce and enhancing operational efficiency through technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, robotic process automation reduces the administrative burden on Child Protection Officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, as mentioned in an op-ed in Lianhe Zaobao, the challenges we face present an opportunity to strengthen and establish a uniquely Singaporean model of family services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Underpinning all that we do is our desire to better serve families that we work with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That is why we are working with social service agencies to strengthen the family services sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Prof Tan Tai Yong, President of the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), and I co-chair the Committee to consider ways in which we can deliver services in a more holistic and family-centric manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Indeed, Assoc Prof Razwana Begum, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Fahmi Aliman will be happy to know that one issue the Committee is considering is how we can provide care that meets the complex needs of families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This ensures that families are served in a comprehensive, coordinated and convenient way, instead of being "bounced around" multiple services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over 200 social service professionals shared their views over multiple engagement sessions, and I personally visited each social service agency and heard from many other stakeholders and partners as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To be sure, there are many perspectives on how to strengthen the sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At this juncture, we are keeping an open mind and considering all options and ideas that have been surfaced to us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are committed to this consultative approach of co-creation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We thank all who have shared their views, and we will continue to listen to you.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is a multi-year, iterative process, where we build upon each other's ideas, so that the solutions that we land on are ultimately robust and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our laser focus on better serving our families remains at the heart of what we do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, let us work together, take this sector to the next level, so that we can continue to be that bright beacon of hope, that wind beneath the wings of our families that keeps them safe from the vagaries of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I will now share our progress and upcoming efforts to support PwDs and their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are committed to enabling PwDs to work and live in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our fourth Enabling Masterplan, EMP2030, envisions Singapore in 2030 as a place that includes and empowers persons with disabilities to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To ensure we are on the right track, Mr Ong Hua Han can be assured that we regularly conduct surveys on the well-being and experiences of PwDs, including in the workplace, through the Disability and Inclusion Panel Study (DIPS) and Public Attitudes Study.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These inform our EMP2030 strategies, raise public awareness and promote inclusivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under EMP2030, we want to blunt the post-18 cliff effect that PwDs and their family members face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Therefore, we commit to making progress in two main areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, strengthening support for PwDs to pursue employment and lifelong learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, empowering PwDs to live independently in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Employment is not just about a monthly paycheck.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is also a source of social connection, dignity and it is what many PwDs aspire to, as they apply their skills meaningfully through work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our employment strategy starts upstream, to strengthen work-readiness of students transitioning from school to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For those needing more time to prepare for work after graduation from special education (SPED) schools, we will progressively expand the School-to-Work (S2W) and job support in key sectors that already have or the potential to employ PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond the transition, from school, we are also doing more to support persons with disabilities towards meaningful employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the sectoral level, we are taking a targeted approach to curate job opportunities in six key sectors that either already traditionally hire or can offer suitable jobs to PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And these include F&B, retail trade, health and social services, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Within these sectors, SG Enable will identify and develop inclusive hiring champions among Enabling Mark-accredited companies and SkillsFuture "Queen Bee" companies to engage and inspire others to hire inclusively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2023, we launched the Enabling Business Hub (EBH) at Jurong which is a showcase of inclusive employment in an industry-specific setting, in this case, logistics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua will be happy to note that the EBH provides a longer and more intensive job support for those who need it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the firm level, we want to ensure that employers and workplaces are inclusive, too.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Rachel Ong, Ms Denise Phua and Mr Ong Hua Han asked about this, and we do so by providing support through multiple approaches, legal protections, wage offsets, workplace modifications, capability building and recognition frameworks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, in the legal domain, we have strengthened protections for persons with disabilities through the Workplace Fairness Bill that was passed in this House a few months ago.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Carrie Tan will also be pleased to know that the tripartite partners are developing a Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations to raise awareness and guide employers in adjusting jobs or work environments to better support PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second the Government provides wage offsets to firms that hire PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, employers who are keen to hire PwDs may need to purchase equipment or modify the workplace or job scope.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We encourage this and provide the Job Redesign Grant to defray the costs of these modifications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Fourth, to foster an inclusive workplace culture, it is important to build confidence and skills to interact with, integrate and include PwDs at the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Training grants and workshops are available to organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Fifth, we recognise and benchmark firms for their best practices and outcomes in disability-inclusive employment via the Enabling Mark Accreditation framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lastly, those unable to work are also not left behind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Instead, we enhance their opportunities for lifelong learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, such PwDs are engaged by multiple services, such as Day Activity Centres and Sheltered Workshops.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the Enabling Skills for Life Programme, PwDs will be better served with a single service catering to their evolving learning needs and they will benefit from a curriculum focused on independent living, communication and language, and social-emotional skills, without needing to move between multiple services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our second key thrust of support is to empower PwDs to live and participate in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ann is a former client of TOUCH Ubi Hostel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After leaving the hostel, she continued participating in TOUCH's outreach programmes but was only able to do so infrequently due to a long commute.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since October last year, the new Enabling Services Hub (ESH) @ Jurong has brought opportunities closer to where she lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I recently met Ann at Taman Jurong CC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Like my son, Ann loves collecting Pokémon cards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, I promptly suggested catching up over a happy meal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From our conversation, I learnt that Ann works part-time at Subway, takes part in continual education and learning courses and makes friends by volunteering at ESH@Jurong's events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Staying in a job and being in touch with the community have bolstered Ann's her self-confidence, empowering her to lead an independent and fulfilling life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We want to support PwDs like Ms Ann to live independently in our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is an area that Ms Denise Phua is interested in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, most PwDs live with their families and would like to continue doing so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, many have ageing caregivers who may soon be unable to care for them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Without other options, they may end up institutionalised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, a person with physical disabilities may live with a caregiver who is frail and unable to provide support with daily living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This family could tap on the Home Support Programme's visiting services, such as monitoring and coaching for independent living and social skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Other PwDs are not able to live with their families and may need additional support for their residential arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, a PwD who is earning a lower income and whose aged caregivers have passed may be concerned about long-term living arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under the Enabled Living Programme, such lower-income clients will live in designated public rental flats, and receive support, such as basic supervision, referrals to financial assistance, and coaching on living and social skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond new community living models, we will strengthen enablers for independent living, starting with assistive technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, PwDs go to touchpoints, such as at public hospitals and social service agencies, for an assistive technology assessment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These centres will be key touchpoints allowing PwDs to undergo assessment for straightforward assistive technology needs and to gather more assistive technology information and resources, while Tech Able, jointly managed by SG Enable and SPD, continue to play a central role supporting PwDs for specialised assistive technology needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Another key enabler is providing convenient services and opportunities for PwDs to participate in local communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To that end, we have begun operations at two more Enabling Services Hubs (ESHs) in Jurong, as previously mentioned, and Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ESHs provide a regional touchpoint for PwDs and caregivers, providing crucial information and referral services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Carrie Tan asked how we are facilitating the integration of PwDs in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ESHs provide opportunities for PwDs and the community to come together through activities, such as sports, gardening or volunteering.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With two new ESHs, there are now more opportunities for interaction between PwDs and wider society, which is key to enabling them to participate in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Lastly, as Prime Minister Wong announced, we will increase subsidies for adult disability services and extend them to more households with effect from next year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This helps defray the cost of services and devices for PwDs and their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, Singapore is our motherland and home, and many Singaporeans hope that Singapore becomes a more loving, inclusive and beautiful home, full of opportunities where all families can thrive, regardless of the challenges they face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For lower-income families, we are not only increasing our assistance through enhancements to ComCare, but also empowering families through ComLink+ to help these families to achieve independence and a stable life, breaking the vicious cycle of poverty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In our latest slate of enhancements to ComLink+, we are integrating services across the health and housing landscapes to enable families to access support in these two areas more easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For PwDs, we are making strides to increase their employment opportunities after school and lifelong learning channels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the same time, we have launched a series of pilot programmes, such as the Enabled Living Programme, Home Support Programme and Enabling Skills for Life Programme to provide PwDs with more choices and support, helping them fulfil their aspirations to live independently in the community for the long term. : Chair, allow me to conclude by observing that many societies around the world today are becoming more and more divided.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This occurs because those facing difficulties feel that society works against and not for them, and their efforts do not result in progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this is exactly why MSF strives to make Singapore a place where all families thrive, regardless of their challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But to be sure, we cannot do this alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All of us have a part to play, whether by volunteering to support lower-income families or being inclusive towards the PwDs that we see in our communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: By extending a helping hand, we enrich our lives but, at the same time, we also strengthen our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We create a society of opportunities and hope, where all are empowered to realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We become the Singapore we want to be.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singapore's Diamond Jubilee is an occasion to renew our commitment to our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In MSF, we remain dedicated to nurturing and building lives together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister of State Sun has spoken on our efforts to build strong families and provide every child a good start; and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua has spoken on our efforts to empower lower-income households and PwDs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, I would like to summarise with three key messages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, how far we have come and the core principles that undergird MSF's work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, what lies ahead for us, and our vision for the social service sector and our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And third, the important role our social service professionals play.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is within families that our values and character are shaped and where we find joy as well as support in times of trouble.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A strong family is, therefore, able to nurture children to fulfil their potential and contribute meaningfully to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why our policies emphasise the role of the family in the life of the individual and are aimed at building strong and resilient families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we adopt a strengths-based perspective in our work with families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families have the strengths and resilience needed to overcome challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The role of the community and the Government is to journey along with them, guiding them to harness their strengths in a meaningful manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We begin early by laying good foundations for the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Where issues start to arise, we aim to address them upstream to prevent issues from getting worse.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Downstream, problems can escalate and are often more complex to resolve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We equip parents with an understanding of maternal health and parenting strategies, so that they are more empowered in bringing up their children well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To amplify the impact, a whole-of-society approach is necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We weave together a network of support by fostering collaboration between different partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes our social service agencies and professionals, academics and corporates.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The expertise and strength of this network enhances the support provided to families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Families for Life @ Community initiative is one such example.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It brings together partners such as social service agencies, religious organisations and community groups to foster a family-friendly environment in each town.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This allows families to enjoy family-bonding activities and marriage, and parenting courses and programmes close to their home.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The principles of family-centricity, strengths-based and proactiveness have laid a strong foundation in recent years and delivered good outcomes for our families, and we will remain guided by these principles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Next, I would like to talk about what lies ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The challenges in the years ahead have been discussed extensively in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will face demographic changes, manpower constraints and increasingly complex social issues, amongst other challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Rapid technological developments will also have an impact on the needs of our families and certainly on our social services manpower and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These challenges present us too with the opportunity to rise to the occasion as a society and as a social service sector and re-imagine the way that we operate and approach issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is our opportunity to build our future together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a sector, one that is dynamic and forward-looking; and as a society, one that comes together to provide opportunities for all.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We envision a social service sector that is dynamic, forward-looking and future-oriented, that is that is agile and responsive to the evolving needs of families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will achieve this vision by strengthening the sector in two ways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we must boldly re-imagine the way we structure and operate our services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The proposed amendments will provide NCSS with the mandate to continue to build the sector’s capabilities, strengthen service delivery and build a stronger ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, NCSS is actively improving social service delivery by strengthening collaboration amongst sector partners and enabling users to find the support they need more easily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also transform our services, to meet the changing needs of our families, and to be more responsive to support those with complex needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua earlier shared that we are undertaking the Family Services Landscape Review.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Representatives from the sector are joining hands with MSF to consider how our social service agencies (SSAs) deliver services and social service professionals can work together to achieve better outcomes for the families we serve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will not rush the process, and we appreciate and recognise the diversity or perspectives and views.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will journey hand-in-hand with all our SSAs and work closely with all of you to strengthen the sector and improve our services.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the more vulnerable among us residing in our social residential homes, we must continue to uplift the quality of care for them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the years, MSF has worked closely with our social residential homes to raise standards of care for residents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, the Bill provides for the possibility of homes evolving to meet residents’ needs, where different client profiles could be housed together.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF and NCSS will also invest in supporting, training and capability building for SSAs operating the homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond residential services, we are also committed to enhancing support for vulnerable individuals in other areas, as Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim has raised.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our efforts are tailored to meet the needs of different groups in a culturally sensitive and effective manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This enables us to create stable, caring environments for all.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, we focus on connecting children in care with nurturing family environments.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We work with fostering agencies to recruit and train foster families to best meet the child’s needs and provide ongoing support for the children and their foster families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For women with young children who have experienced violence, we provide safe shelters and trauma-informed care to support them through difficult times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also provide employment assistance and referrals to preschool services for their children to facilitate mothers’ return to the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we must harness the power of research and data in tackling issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling will be pleased to hear that we have deepened our collaboration with sector practitioners, and local and regional academics.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This builds up our body of knowledge and helps us better design and evaluate our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF partnered the Centre for Research on Successful Ageing at Singapore Management University (SMU) and the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) at National University of Singapore (NUS), to understand societal perspectives on essential household needs and how society can support less privileged Singaporeans to meet these needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This study informed the recent review of ComCare assistance rates, as shared by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must continue to facilitate the sharing of best practices regionally and internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We can benefit other communities by providing thought leadership in areas where we have done well.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the Asian Family Conference 2024, various academics and practitioners shared Singapore's efforts in working with families and our approach to social issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These resonated with local and regional researchers, policy-makers and practitioners, and inspired their thinking on similar challenges they face in their own communities and countries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also be hosting two conferences this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In April, we are partnering IPS to hold the inaugural International Conference for Societies of Opportunity to discuss how countries can do more to address the important issue of social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In July, NCSS will host the Social Service Summit.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, for the first time, we will also invite social service leaders from the region to facilitate connections and enrich our learning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By boldly re-imagining, transforming or restructuring the way we work, and creating platforms for sharing and collaboration, we will forge a social sector that is dynamic and forward looking.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, beyond the social service sector, we aim to build a society of opportunities through a collective effort, where all Singaporeans will have opportunities to flourish.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We all have a role in creating this society of opportunities and must collectively uplift the members of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These community contributions complement Government funding for social services, which has grown over the years, allowing us to make a greater impact and invest more to build the sector’s capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For our corporates, it means including corporate social responsibility as part of their business strategy and aligning their corporate purpose with their social mission.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am encouraged that more are stepping forward.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I was also heartened to hear that at the recent travel fair, the National Association of Travel Agencies (NATAS), encouraged people to donate generously to communities in need and even displayed the ComChest donation QR code throughout the event hall.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Employers like Sheng Shiong, MoneyMax and Changi Airport Group have embraced SGSHARE.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, they can bring close to 6,000 employees into our community of givers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened that small and medium enterprises (SMEs), such as Bright Point International and Red Beacon Asset Management, have also come onboard SGSHARE.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This demonstrates that big or small, all businesses can play a part.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
