text: At the community-level, individual efforts are organised for maximum impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have moved beyond individual ad hoc volunteering towards sustained and more impactful volunteering.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The MSFCare Network now has more than 4,000 active volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through the Network, volunteering is personalised based on volunteers’ skills and interest, such as in mentoring or mobilising new volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More individuals are volunteering regularly, and this coordinated effort has meant that we are better able to achieve greater impact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the individual-level, many have also contributed through generous donations and we see more individuals donating directly to ComChest.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We encourage individuals to continue to play their part through regular and sustained giving.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Melvin Yong noted that everyone must play their part in uplifting fellow citizens, particularly our vulnerable and low-income groups, as part of our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will amplify the impact of donations made towards key social programmes, supporting those with more needs in our community, including low-income families, PwDs, children and youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The ComLink+ Progress Packages and KidSTART are some examples.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Several corporate partners have already come forward to donate to these programmes and we want to encourage more Singaporeans to join us in uplifting families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Alongside nationwide programmes, the matching grant will also benefit community-led initiatives identified by ComChest, President’s Challenge or the Collective.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond programme funding, the Government is also studying further support for SSAs and the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In recognition of this, we have dedicated 2025 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the sector, the road ahead will be an exciting one.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have been presented with the opportunity to reimagine the way we operate and support our families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To achieve this, we need to continue to invest in supporting and uplifting our social service professionals at each stage of their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To questions raised by Mr Keith Chua and Mr Baey Yam Keng, we are committed to offering attractive pathways for professional growth and development.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we are committed to ensuring the competency of the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This starts by equipping social service professionals for their roles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Assoc Prof Razwana's question, we work with Institutes of Higher Learning and SSAs to ensure curriculum and training programmes are relevant and based on industry needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Once our professionals enter the workforce, they can stage their development based on the Skills Framework for Social Service, which lays out the required competencies and progression pathways.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Much learning takes place on the job and conducted by employers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, Child Protection Officers receive skills-based training, structured supervision and peer support to equip them for the challenges of their work.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Keith Chua will be happy to know that we will provide more opportunities for passionate individuals to make a mid-career switch into the social service sector, such as through our Career Conversion Programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Melvin Yong's query, we have been steadily increasing the Skills and Salary Guidelines to be competitive with the market and commensurate with the professionals' contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have been engaging employers to strengthen adherence with the guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The work in social services can be demanding, as Assoc Prof Razwana and Ms Carrie Tan noted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will work with SSAs and empower SSA leaders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, the Social Service Institute's courses on organisational development equip SSA leaders to create a supportive work environment where our professionals feel valued, respected and empowered.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS also rolled out support for SSAs to conduct Employee Engagement Survey so that they take active steps to improve staff engagement and well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS also provides social service professionals with training on self-care and resilience, and a Sabbatical Leave Scheme to recharge.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In MSF, for example, Child Protection Officers experiencing high levels of stress are granted time-off, and those requiring additional support are referred for specialised intervention.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, the sector must continue to reward and recognise those who have contributed significantly to the cause.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is my hope that, through all these efforts, the sector will constantly innovate new practices and approaches, and ultimately, to improve service delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are many who are already doing so.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr D Senthil Kumar, from the Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore, has been instrumental in integrating innovative technologies into physiotherapy to improve patient outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, he was involved in introducing an advanced treadmill leveraging virtual reality for balance and motor function training in cerebral palsy rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With this, Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore's clients feel more motivated and engaged and are able to achieve their therapy outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Kumar's work inspires us to constantly innovate and upskill so that we can achieve better outcomes for those we serve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The social service sector offers a future with potential and rewarding opportunities and we seek to inspire more Singaporeans to join.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay. :   Families are the roots that grounds our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They shape the values, well-being and future of our communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Akin to roots that support trees to grow with resilience, when we strengthen families, we will also strengthen our society as a whole.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A strong family is able to nurture children to fulfil their potential and contribute meaningfully to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Support should not only be available when issues become too complex for families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Instead, we proactively link families up with community resources early.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Cinta Abadi (Eternal Love) programme sets the stage for soon-to-wed Malay/Muslim couples to have effective communication and encourage them to discuss about managing expectations and challenges early.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also strengthen the social sector so that we are responsive to evolving needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will work closely with the sector to re-imagine the social services landscape to uplift the quality of care of the Social Residential Homes and strengthen NCSS’ role as a sector developer.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These efforts to strengthen families are also made possible by the contributions of our social service professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to make social service a career of choice and a sector that attracts and nurtures talent. : Mr Chairman, through our efforts over the recent years, together with our sector partners and professionals, we have made good progress in empowering resilient and thriving families in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to strengthen families through family-centred, strength-based and proactive initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Looking ahead, we are excited to embark on this journey to collectively see, shape and build a social service sector that is dynamic and forward-looking, and a society of opportunities for all in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am confident that with the strong capabilities we have built up in our sector professionals and academic community, Singapore can become a thought leader in the social service sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are pioneering unique approaches to tackle complex issues that have inspired others in the regional and international community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we commemorate SG60, let us renew our shared commitment to play our part to build a society full of opportunities for all.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we can build a resilient tomorrow with our collective strengths of today, to build a Singapore where no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Chairman, I thank Minister Masagos, Minister of State Sun Xueling and the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua for their responses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have two clarifications for Minister of State Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I note the progress that we have made in the preschool sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I have some suggestions in my cut and I hope the Minister of State can address them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can we establish a quality assurance framework that regularly assesses all preschools in Singapore and also publish these standards?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Doing so will, hopefully, encourage all preschools in Singapore to raise their standard.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My second question pertains to the retention of preschool teachers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can ECDA conduct a local study to identify and better understand the push factors behind why our preschool teachers are leaving the industry?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My brief interaction with many of these preschool teachers seems to suggest that burnout is a common reason.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are there any plans by MSF to further increase our investments in the professional development of our early childhood educators?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I will touch on the last point first.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I had shared in my main reply that we have put a focus on nurturing a positive preschool and parent partnership in ECDA's refreshed "Shape Our Tomorrow" campaign.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This relationship between parents and teachers is not unique to the preschool sector.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was also something that MOE had talked about, the parent and school partnership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But beyond that, we do have to look at what we can do to address this poor work-life balance issue that has come up through the survey, something that the Member has also mentioned before, and also excessive administrative duties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, first and foremost, to put into context, we have grown the early childhood educators manpower pool by a lot because we wanted to expand our capacity for more preschools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: While we are doing that, we are also going out with reviews, basically, to salaries, because in order to attract educators to join, you must obviously have an attractive sector.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also designated the six preschool closure days as Development Days, to allow the preschools protected time.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also removed the mandatory requirement for childcare centres to operate on Saturdays.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, all that takes into account and puts in place measures to ensure that our early childhood educators have time off.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, coming back to what was shared about the excessive administrative duties, we are also trying to roll out digitalisation initiatives.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, in 2021, ECDA had launched the Early Childhood Industry Digital Plan and also a Digitalisation Grant.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To date, more than 60% of preschools have adopted these digital solutions, including the preschool management system, to help streamline educators' administrative tasks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is a very long-winded answer, I am sorry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But a very last point I would like to add, is that apart from that, we want to make sure that the environment is a conducive one, the physical environment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, what we also have is that we have worked with preschools to see how we can have ergonomic furniture for preschool educators, because I think some mothers around us would know, when you take care of young children, say, for example, infants, some of us have this stiff wrist syndrome.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If you are only taking care of one child and you have the stiff wrist syndrome, imagine if you are an infant educarer and you are taking care of three infants.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, for example, like a little wrist guard, certain things like that and also the furniture – what can we do to make sure the environment is a conducive one for preschool educators and also making sure that they have a designated rest area so that they can have their lunch in peace, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, these are all the various measures we are putting in place to ensure that our preschool educators feel valued, respected and have some downtime for their rest.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When it comes to the framework that the Member had talked about with regard to curriculum, I had talked about SPARK 2.0.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, we also have the Nurturing Early Learners Framework and the Early Years Development Framework.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, all those frameworks are published to ensure that our pedagogical practices, together with the Code of Practice that we have rolled out, ensure that the overall quality standards of the preschool sector are open, transparent and our parents have confidence in the industry.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will try to get through as many as possible.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, please keep it short and likewise, front bench, if you can keep your answers short as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I have just one clarification for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In one of my cuts, I highlighted that adults with invisible neuro-divergent conditions, especially those with lower support needs, they do not receive much institutional support post-education.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I do not think this was addressed earlier, so I would appreciate MSF for sharing if there are any plans to look into this space and develop support measures for these individuals?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I believe many of the schemes that I have talked about in my main speech would apply in the specific instance, especially for workplaces.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But why not do it from within the companies?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think all those would add to making sure that our workplaces have a good chance of becoming more inclusive over time.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because it is not just about setting a quota.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is very much also about making sure that our culture and the softer parts of the workplace can shift in the direction that we want to go.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Attitudes, behaviour, values within society – and I think that will take time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am very thankful for all the good work that is done by the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And I can see that our society and Government is one with heart.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One is regarding the many people with good intent who support the ground, whether grassroots or donors or volunteers, and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I find that on the ground, many of them pounce, in a positive way, on especially families in rental blocks, with food, service, bags, school shoes and everything.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But is there a way that we can better coordinate all these efforts on the ground without discouraging them but encouraging them as well?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My second one is to do with adults with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think at a macro level, as I have mentioned in my Committee of Supply speech, there is really a need to clarify, develop and communicate a continuum of the models, whether in living, working or learning.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mainly because it is just such a diverse spectrum of population.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know that some work has been done, but instead of mentioning things that are maybe more programme-centric, we can really show the community that there is a spectrum and there is a way by which people can be more proactive in assessing their needs, deciding on what models they do, and maybe even work together to develop these models together.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And second is, is there a continuum from the work front, or what are the continuum of working models from sheltered workshops like —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Phua, you want to get your clarification?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Autism Resource Centre's high model at the Enabling Village.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I suppose I will attempt a reply to her first clarification and I suppose I will take it in two parts.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Her first point was really about a broad general comment about how generally the social sector is.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Oftentimes when it is the year-end, festive season, or when it comes to Chinese New Year, or after Ramadan, upcoming is Puasa, you see a lot of goodwill being poured into the rental flat communities.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Here is where I think I want to just point to just one point.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To me, it is really about how the Government, the people sector, the corporate sector and individual volunteers, how all of us can pitch in and better coordinate our resources.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because if we just leave it be, good things will get done, we will still have a lot of corporates and a lot of self-organised groups and in a way parachuting things onto our rental flat residents, as Ms Denise Phua would have characterised it.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But that is possibly not the best way to organise ourselves.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is also possibly not the best way we can maximise the potential of our giving.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I will just make one clarion call and that is for all stakeholders involved – Government, community, people sector, private sector, individual volunteers – to come together to really work together to be sure that our efforts at alleviating poverty, at helping to uplift Singaporean families can have an outsized and multiplier effect when we go out together.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think we will be stronger for it.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is my first reply to her first clarification.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: My second reply pertains perhaps more to the disability sector.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think she is also trying to allude to the fact that we have so many programmes and so many pilots now.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To me, that is a testament and reflection of the challenges that we face in providing for the sector in a sense that we have the different disability groups, the disability types – sensory impairments, physical disabilities, neuro-divergence, visible, invisible – and everything occurs on a spectrum.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And her point about how we can get everyone to see all these different pilots on a spectrum, I think we are not quite there yet in terms of forming a thoughtful continuum of services, if you will.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I do not think we are at a stage where we are sufficiently mature to say that we have possibly covered all and at the same time, from the resource, resource deployment and management perspectives, maximised our outcomes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think it is a little bit early days; we will still need to evolve some of these pilots as we go along to make sure that we can possibly see a much more thoughtful and well-managed spectrum of services that we will see hopefully, in time to come.

speaker: The Chairman
text: There are four more Members so make it quick.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling, get straight to your clarification, please.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just want to say a quick note of thanks to Minister, political office holders —

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think just get straight to the clarification.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: — everyone in social services who are working very hard to help our Singaporeans in need.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The first one is on social service research.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: In the 18 years that I spent in NCSS on social service, I have learned that social interventions, especially for complex needs, do take time, sometimes years to see effect.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: If not, are there plans to do so and for which group?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I just wanted to check where is the location of this hub and what are the mental health services put together?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We thank Ms Ng Ling Ling for the clarification questions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the second question, it is a joint project with MOH.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary mentioned it yesterday.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They are still working out where to put it and what the norms and delivery of the service would be like.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To address the first question, for the last five years, since I came onboard, I have been meeting many researchers from various Institutes of Higher Learning and I discovered that they are really a trove of knowledge, experience, data.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some of the data are in MSF and one of the complaints they do have is that they cannot publish it and therefore, they cannot establish themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have a great opportunity to put all these together and involve them together with MSF to even establish our own body of knowledge, one that is Singapore's body of knowledge on social science and social service sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is quite a daring venture because we did not do it internally, we put it out in the open, with statistically sound methodology, get it challenged, presented it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If you work on a preschool child today, you already know even the initial outcome, maybe 10, if not 15 years later.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And then, onwards, beyond that, was there really impact on the work we did to the to the development of the person as an adult, for example?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are really interesting questions to ask and to research on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are very happy they are onboard and they will help us with this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Actually, I am also very happy that in the last Asian Family Conference we signed a commitment with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states, who endorsed a research collaboration.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This research collaboration allows SUSS to go out into the region to work with various institutes of higher learning in the ASEAN member states to study the state of the families in ASEAN.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Carrie Tan, straight to your clarification, please.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Clarification two would be regarding Senior Parliamentary Chua's speech on the Enabling Hubs at Jurong and Punggol.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And contrary to Ms Denise Phua, I do not like to keep talking about needs and challenges.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I want to ask what is the Ministry currently doing to raise awareness about the strengths and potential contributions that our PwDs and PWSNs can contribute to society, instead of always perpetuating the narrative about their needs and their challenges.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The fourth clarification is to Minister Masagos regarding the NCSS implementing employee engagement surveys in SSAs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: My question is: are these employee engagement surveys meant for internal review purposes or will they also be required to submit that to NCSS?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And will there be an independent panel or channel for SSA personnel to whistle blow or to raise the alarm on any kind of unhelpful management practices that are causing them distress at work?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: Mr Eric Chua: Sir, it is not so much the Enabling Services Hubs, but the Enabling Business Hub.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: Actually, we support businesses of all sizes, including SMEs in inclusive hiring.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: At the EBH at Jurong, they have also engaged local business communities, like the Federation of Merchants' Association, Singapore; Bukit Gombak Traders' Association and Taman Jurong Hawkers' Association, to reach out to the neighbourhood shops to try to promote inclusive hiring.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: On the Member's third clarification, I believe it is about awareness.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: This is co-chaired by myself and Mr Adrian Tan, Chairman of Ad Planet Group, to really support the "i'mable" movement, the public education initiative by SG Enable, and Ms Carrie Tan has mentioned in previous Sittings before about the power of stories, and exactly, the "i'mable" public education initiative works with partners to highlight the strengths and contributions of PwDs through storytelling, media representations and collaborations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Punggol West)
text: And we feature individuals, such as the Goh Chok Tong Enable Awards, with Mediacorp and also, at the same time, we hope to change mindsets and deepen the DNA of inclusion in Singapore society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Actually, I am a little confused by Ms Carrie Tan's question.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the survey, it is specifically for improving work environment, engagement with employees, and this is used as a tool for the SSAs to improve their organisation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At this point of time, it is not necessary for them to put it back to NCSS because it is a tool for them to use.

speaker: The Chairman
text: For those who raise single cuts, I am sorry, we have run out of time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, can I invite Mr Melvin Yong, if you would like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Chairman, I thank the Minister and the MSF team for addressing the wide range of issues that Members have raised.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: As we navigate through these challenging times, I am heartened that MSF and the social service sector are doing their best to support vulnerable Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: They remind us of the strength of unity and the power of collective action as we foster a more caring society where everyone has the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their starting point.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Chairman, with that, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Head I, Ministry of Social and Family Development.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Economic stability, social welfare, educational opportunities, social mobility, community engagement and expectations around healthcare and housing all come together to form the social compact that binds us together as one united nation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Over the past 60 years, our strong social compact has been instrumental in fostering a sense of national identity, unity and collective responsibility among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As Singapore commemorates 60 years of Independence, we must continue to ensure that our economic policies benefit all segments of society.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This includes investing in skills training, supporting local small and medium enterprises, and creating jobs that cater to different skill levels.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But there remain barriers to upward mobility for low-income families, with entrenched inequalities affecting education and job opportunities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How can we better support low-income families in education, skills training and job placement to break the cycles of poverty?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is crucial that we continue to provide equitable access to opportunities, to reduce income inequality and ensure opportunities for all segments of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must continue to review and to update our social support schemes for our vulnerable populations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some segments may still fall through the gaps, such as gig workers or freelancers who may not qualify for the traditional safety nets.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With an ageing population, there are also concerns about the sustainability of our existing social support schemes and the adequacy of retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Social service agencies, such as the Family Service Centres, play a critical role in supporting vulnerable families in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am concerned about attracting quality professionals into the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The National Council of Social Service (NCSS) regularly releases salary guidelines for job roles in the social service sector.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How can we better support the financial sustainability of our social service ecosystem, so that they are not overly dependent on Government grants?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How can we encourage more Singaporeans to donate regularly to our social service agencies and also encourage more volunteerism?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond uplifting the social service sector, I would like to encourage the Ministry to place greater emphasis on supporting families with complex issues, as part of our refreshed Forward Singapore social compact.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the Ministry’s plan to enhance the ways in which the social service sector delivers its services and programmes so that vulnerable families, in particular families with multiple and complex needs, can be better supported?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should also do more to encourage active citizenship and promote volunteerism to instill a sense of responsibility towards the collective well-being.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the Ministry’s plan to further encourage individual Singaporeans and the community to step up their efforts in contributing to society?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We have barely turned the page on the pandemic and we are now suddenly faced with a confluence of geopolitical, economic and technological forces, which threatens to create a very uncertain future.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As Singapore commemorates 60 years of Independence, it is crucial that we continue to build a more resilient and supportive society, a future where the social compact is continually reinforced and one in which no Singaporean will be left behind as Singapore progresses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's preschool education is generally regarded as high quality, due to substantial Government investment and a strong regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Research has shown that children receiving quality early childhood education tend to have better cognitive and socio-economic outcomes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must therefore strive to continually enhance the quality of early childhood education in Singapore, both in terms of curriculum standards and teacher standards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is complemented by the Nurturing Early Learners Framework, which guides the teaching and learning in preschools for children aged four to six.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can the Ministry share the adoption rate of both frameworks among preschools in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What are the reasons provided by those preschools that have declined to adopt these frameworks?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can we establish a quality assurance framework that regularly assesses all preschools in Singapore and publish these standards?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Doing so will encourage all preschools in Singapore to raise their standards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: On teacher standards, Singapore has invested heavily to enhance the quality of our preschool teachers through structured training and regulatory frameworks for early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can ECDA conduct a local study to understand the push factors behind why these teachers leave the industry?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Preschool education in Singapore is recognised as a crucial stage in a child's development, preparing them for formal schooling and lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Government has been actively working to enhance the preschool sector through ECDA, which oversees the quality and accessibility of preschool services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Initiatives like the Anchor Operator Scheme and Partner Operator Scheme have been introduced to increase the number of quality preschool places and make them more affordable.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Despite these efforts, the challenge remains to balance affordability with maintaining high standards of care and education across all preschools to support child development and assist working parents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How will the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) further improve the affordability and quality of preschool for all families in Singapore?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In Singapore, the Government recognises the fundamental role of families and aims to create a supportive environment for them.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This involves implementing policies and initiatives that encourage strong family bonds, such as work-life harmony, flexible work arrangements requests and inclusivity within the community.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: MSF has come a long way in enhancing family services, promoting family-friendly workplaces and ensuring that all members of society, including the less privileged and those with special needs, feel included and supported.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These efforts are part of a broader strategy to maintain a cohesive and resilient society.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How will the MSF further build and foster a family-friendly and inclusive Singapore?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will the MSF be further engaging with whole-of-society stakeholders, such as employers and the trade unions to provide more marriage and parenting resources for families?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many sacrifice their careers, drain their savings and push through exhaustion, and sometimes even abuse, to care for their loved ones, often at the expense of their own well-being.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Without them, the healthcare burden on the state will be far greater.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, the current system still assumes that caregiving is a private responsibility, with the Government only coming in to provide relief.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We need a fundamental shift in recognising family caregiving as essential work that deserves proper compensation, not just relief.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Caregiving should be a shared responsibility between individuals, family and society, with its costs partially socialised, rather than falling mainly on caregivers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: A national certification framework should be introduced to provide formal training and better employment opportunities for caregivers, especially after they return to the workforce.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Caregivers are the backbone of our long-term care system.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If we truly value their contributions, we must compensate them fairly.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is not just about doing more, but doing things differently to prepare Singapore for an ageing society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In my Adjournment Motion six years ago, I shared the story of Emma, a single unwed parent who came to see me at my Meet-the-People Sessions, together with her two-month-old daughter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I shared previously, when I asked why Emma did not shed a tear, she told me that she no longer had any tears left.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was simply looking for a roof over her head and her baby's head.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that single unwed parents can finally rent and buy a flat from HDB.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Emma finally got her rental flat, and I am glad to share she finally purchased her very own Build-To-Order (BTO), but the playing field is still not level.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The cash is a lifeline for them, and all these will help reduce the stigma and discrimination that single unwed parents face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Building a family-friendly Singapore requires a multifaceted approach that places a strong emphasis on education, inclusivity and support for diverse family structures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Recognising that families comes in many forms, it is essential to create an environment where every family feels valued and supported.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In this context, how is the Ministry addressing the evolving definition of families to ensure policies and programmes are inclusive of diverse family structure in Singapore?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: How does the Ministry plan to engage with parents, educators and community leaders to reinforce the value of family bonds and relationships among children and teenagers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: What resources and support systems are available for children from non-traditional family backgrounds, to ensure they feel included and valued within the broader community?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And what measures are being taken to support fathers in playing their role effectively within the family and how is the Ministry encouraging paternal involvement in child-rearing and family activities?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Effective support for vulnerable and disadvantaged families and individuals living with multiple and complex needs requires a targeted, coordinated, holistic and multi-agency and personalised response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, it is also important to address the root causes of vulnerability and disadvantage, such as poverty, mental health issues, underemployment, violence and access to housing and education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In this context, what are the Ministry's plans for improving the delivery of services and programmes in the social service sector, to better support vulnerable and disadvantaged families and individuals living with multiple and complex needs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: What initiatives are in place to assist women who have experienced violence, including those with children, access safe accommodation and other resources, and to return to the workforce?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: What initiatives are in place to provide culturally appropriate and sensitive support and assistance, to vulnerable and disadvantaged families and individuals living with multiple and complex needs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: How is the Ministry working to improve the short-, medium- and long-term outcomes for children in care and those with child protection system, and what strategies are in place to ensure that these children have access to timely, stable, long-term and fully supported out of home placements.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In my Budget speech three years ago, I shared about how social workers were overworked and many were burnt out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I said: "Being a social worker is not easy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is like riding a bike, except the bike is on fire.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Everything is on fire." Three years on, and social workers continue to share with me about their crazy workloads and how not much has changed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I tried to have lunch with a social worker and for the entire hour, he was outside the restaurant trying to help a client's family over the phone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In the end, he packed his lunch, and I doubt he had time to eat it later on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Over the past 10 years in Nee Soon East, I have seen so many children's lives get destroyed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: For me, that has been the most painful part of being a Member of Parliament – to see children get neglected, abused, raped; children whom I have seen grow up over the years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In these cases, the Child Protective Services step in and I am grateful for the work of our Child Protection officers (CPOs).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I hope MSF can also share their plans on how they will increase the manpower and resources at the Child Protective Services.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With Budget 2025, I hope that the measures will bring needed relief to most Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have been more concerned about the impact of higher cost on our lower-income Singaporeans in the past year.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During my visits to residents living in rental blocks in Jalan Kayu, who are receiving MSF ComCare assistance, I sometimes see them having mostly instant noodles and highly processed, preserved canned food.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They tell me that they are trying to stretch the ComCare dollar.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I try my best with donors to augment the Government's ComCare with local welfare projects at the Jalan Kayu Heartstrings, which provides groceries and food items that are as healthy as possible, such ground-up support is subject to donation and in-kind sponsorship that we can garner each time.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HPB has been active in their "My Healthy Plate" outreach, with a collection of easy-to-cook healthy recipes for residents of all races.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Two, does MSF track, with MOH, the chronic diseases prevalence and severity of this group?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Again, can MSF and MOH collaborate on upstream preventive measures to avoid this group of vulnerable Singaporeans from developing serious chronic diseases that will not only plague their already difficult lives to further downward spiral, but also cause heavy downstream burdens to our healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Mr Chairman, the ComLink+ scheme, introduced in 2023, pairs vulnerable families with dedicated family coaches and volunteer befrienders who will journey with the families in achieving stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF provide an update on the progress and effectiveness of the ComLink+ scheme?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: While ComLink+ provides financial assistance, there remains a lack of comprehensive services covering mental health, career counselling and social integration.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Are there plans by MSF to introduce partnerships with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the private sector to provide skill development workshops, mental health resources and counselling services tailored to the needs of the ComLink+ families?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can MSF work with relevant service providers to develop tailored financial literacy programmes to help the families make informed decisions about budgeting, saving and investing?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I also invite MSF to collaborate with the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute to implement programmes that include pathways to employment, skills enhancement and career advancement to provide these families with a sustainable means of income over time.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: For children in primary and secondary schools, can MSF collaborate with the schools to provide academic support such as tutoring, mentorship programmes and enrichment classes to ensure that children from ComLink+ families have equal opportunities for success?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Some families may also lack access to technology resources that can facilitate learning and application processes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: ComLink+ is a whole-of-society effort led by the Government but implemented in partnership with the community.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I hope that we can continue to expand the ComLink+ ecosystem to better support lower-income families in their efforts towards building a better future for themselves.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, for any advanced economy, keeping social mobility alive is a key challenge.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Fighting what we call sticky floors and sticky ceilings, and breaking not just the chain of transmission of disadvantages for those at the bottom, but also the transmission of advantages for those at the top, from generation to generation, is tough and is an uphill battle.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I am glad that in Singapore, we have a government that is determined to keep social mobility alive and keep social mobility an integral part of the Singapore Story going forward.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We will need to mitigate unequal opportunities at birth, indeed, before birth, and through life.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It will take dealing with the hand that folks are dealt by life.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: This is why ComLink+ is so important – focusing on families in rental housing, getting them to send their children to preschool, stay in good jobs and build savings, and rewarding them with financial support for such positive behaviours, ultimately, helping to equalise opportunities for their children, and getting coaches and volunteers to journey with them.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If ComCare is assistance to meet today's needs, ComLink+ is empowerment to build tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: If ComCare is a safety net provided by the state, ComLink+ is a new trampoline, formed not just by the state but by all of us.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: To keep social mobility alive, we need ComLink+ to work.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry share an update on the response to date?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can the Ministry provide more details and the timelines for each package?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Overall, how many families have actually benefited from the ComLink+ Progress packages?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is the average number of families that a family coach handles?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has the Ministry been able to recruit its target number of family coaches so far?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, while Singapore has established strong social safety nets to support vulnerable individuals and families, some low-income households continue to face complex and interlocking challenges in achieving stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Beyond financial assistance, there is a need for a more personalised, empowering approach that helps families take proactive steps towards a better future.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Could MSF share insights on how the ComLink+ ecosystem will better support lower-income families in their journey towards improved life outcomes?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Additionally, what measures are being considered to further empower low-income households in pursuing long-term aspirations for themselves and their children?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, I thank our Prime Minister for signalling his support to look into the needs of persons with disabilities (PwDs), especially after formal schooling.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Why does the community especially families, feel such despair, especially post-age 18?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The answer lies in the lack of continuity in support systems – what is often termed as the "cliff effect" in the disability sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Families are left to navigate a fragmented landscape.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, how can we shift families from a place of helplessness to a place of hope?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These programmes aim to make community, employment and living support more accessible to PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Both the Enabling Services Hub and the Enabling Business Hub have been operational for some time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge the MSF to provide some updates on their current status, achievements, challenges and future plans.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also seek MSF to share the progress of the Enabled Living Programme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, the truth is that the needs of adults with disabilities are diverse.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some require intensive round-the-clock care while others need much less support to build independent living skills.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This diversity therefore calls for a continuum of support models tailored to individual needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On living, one of the most pressing gaps is the lack of long-term residential options for adults with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While I applaud MSF's openness to exploring an Enabled Living Programme for those with mild to moderate needs, we must move beyond programme-centric approaches.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Instead, we need a spectrum of residential models to suit different archetypes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On learning, on the learning front, the situation is also equally urgent.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: When asked about continuing education for PwDs yesterday, the Ministry of Education (MOE) has indicated that MSF and SG Enable will take the lead, citing the diverse and complex needs of this population.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This abrupt decline in structured training opportunities leads to skill loss, reduced independence and increased burdens on families and society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The problem is compounded in a world where technology is rapidly disrupting all our lives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Additionally, I propose the establishment of lifelong learning colleges for major disability groups, partnering with social service agencies that have a proven track record in this space.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Work provides dignity, identity, financial independence and purpose.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: With proper training and support, PwDs can contribute meaningfully to workplaces and society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: During the recent Workplace Fairness Bill discussion, I proposed the creation of a job accommodation network – a resource to guide employers in implementing reasonable accommodations and to empower PwDs themselves with self-advocacy skills.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This would help them balance their needs with employers' business constraints.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While MOM may have other priorities, I really urge the Ministry to work with its partners to take the lead on this initiative.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, extend job placement and job support for PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is not sufficient as PwDs often require long-term assistance to navigate workplace challenges.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Stopping support after one year is akin to removing eyeglasses from someone with myopia, leaving them unable to see clearly.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some of these groups really need longer support.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In a rapidly changing job market, relevance is key.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Jobs that exist today may disappear tomorrow and PwDs must be equipped with the skills to adapt.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Four, include sheltered workshops as part of a continuum of employment models.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Sheltered workshops hold strong potential as a viable employment model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is actually less costly than the Day Activity Centres and it offers a more focused and purposeful alternative to Day Activity Centres, which can be costly and lack an emphasis on work.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Ministry should also clarify and communicate the continuum of employment models available to PwDs, their families and other stakeholders so as to enable them to make informed decisions about the most suitable employment model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While the School-To-Work scheme by MOE for recent SPED school graduates is a good initiative, the earliest SPED graduates and mainstream graduates with special educational needs are often overlooked.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge the Government to allocate resources to address that gap and ensure that no one is excluded.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I look forward to serving with you to support the disability community.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: An inclusive society ensures that every individual, regardless of ability, has the opportunity to contribute meaningfully.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: It is about dignity, independence and social integration.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Unlocking our workforce's full potential drives growth for businesses, strengthens communities and fuels national progress.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Coming from the private sector, I have witnessed first-hand the collective will and efforts of the Government, MSF, SG Enable, social service agencies and enterprises, commercial or otherwise, all working together to advance inclusive hiring.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For this, I am thankful – to see our shared commitment to the cause translating bit by bit into meaningful opportunities for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Persons with disabilities and their caregivers have long-term aspirations, just like anyone else.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They want to actively participate in shared spaces, secure meaningful employment and live independently within the community.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We have come a long way in providing more pathways for persons with disabilities to thrive.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, there is always more that can be done.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I had previously called for more support in the post-18 space and I am delighted to hear it specifically highlighted in the Budget by the Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Now that we are debating in the Committee of Supply (COS), can MSF share more about how it plans to strengthen support structures for persons with disabilities as they transition from school to work?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, we also need to recognise the crucial role that caregivers play.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They are the unseen pillar of strength, often putting their needs and dreams on hold to care for their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I am very glad that the update to the Home Caregiving Grant, as announced in the Budget Statement, will extend financial support to more caregivers and affirm their contributions.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While this is highly appreciated, caregivers also face emotional strain, physical exhaustion and the challenge of looking after their own well-being.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Building on this, can MSF also share its plans to further support caregivers beyond financial assistance?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Last year, I spoke about recalibrating our means-testing criteria for disability schemes, at the MSF COS.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Reading this year's Budget annexes, I understand that the means-testing criteria will be revised for the better.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Examples include the Assistive Technology Fund, the Enabling Transport Subsidy and Taxi Subsidy Scheme, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I have previously suggested that the threshold should at least align with the current median PCHI figures.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Assuming that median PCHI grows steadily, the harmonised threshold of $4,800 should exceed that level.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I am pleased to see this update go beyond my initial suggestion to broaden access to support schemes.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I urge MSF to continually review the PCHI threshold at timely intervals to ensure that it keeps pace with median PCHI levels as they rise.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Following this progress, I would like to reiterate my call from last year that we also take into account actual costs borne by families with PwDs.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Financial support schemes should reflect the real and often higher costs that these families face.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: By doing so, we empower more persons with disabilities to live with dignity and achieve their dreams.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Chair, we need to better support working adults who are neurodivergent.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Over the years we have made progress in increasing support for neurodivergent students through special educational needs officers and school counsellors.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Neurodivergent conditions such as autism, ADHD and dyslexia last a lifetime.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, beyond school, existing policies and programmes cater only to autistic individuals, mainly those with high support needs.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: A large proportion of neurodivergent adults are left to navigate life's challenges without institutional support when they enter the workforce.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This is especially true for those with conditions such as ADHD and dyslexia, which are invisible and not formally recognised as disabilities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They may struggle with organisation, executive function, or navigating workplace expectations.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Many are also hesitant to ask for accommodations or help, fearing stigma or uncertainty about how employers will respond.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I urge the Ministry to take action in two key areas.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: First, in order to design effective policies, we need data.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: A national survey can help us to understand how best to support neurodivergent adults in daily life and in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: The Ministry can then craft targeted support measures that are evidence based and impactful.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Second, we need to raise more awareness around neurodiversity, especially in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This can be done through awareness training for both employers and employees.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Such training helps address common misconceptions around neurodivergent conditions.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: It also offers a platform to facilitate open discussion on potential workplace adjustments that can both accommodate neurodivergent employees and play to their strengths.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: On top of raising sufficient awareness, we must also ensure safe and fair disclosure practises and combat stigma.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Similar to mental health conditions, perhaps the Government could introduce an advisory on providing support for employees with neurodivergent conditions.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Chairman, I rise today to speak on an issue we all intuitively agree on – a more inclusive society where persons with disabilities and special needs (PWSNs), whom I prefer to call differently-abled, are recognised not for their limitations, but for their strengths and contributions.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We must deliberate steps to ensure that inclusivity is not just a concept but a lived reality.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Misconceptions and stereotypes about disabilities persist largely due to a lack of understanding.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We must launch public awareness campaigns that highlight the strengths, talents and capabilities of PWSNs, showcasing their success stories in business, sports, the arts and technology.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: These campaigns should feature real-life stories of perseverance and excellence, demonstrating that ability transcends disability.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: By shifting public perception, we empower PWSNs with dignity and opportunities while fostering a society where every individual feels valued.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: The media plays a profound role in shaping societal attitudes.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In October last year, The Inclusive Code was launched in New Zealand.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Media is a mirror of society, and when PwDs and PWSNs see themselves represented positively – whether in advertisements, films or news, they are affirmed.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: More importantly, it normalises disability in everyday life, helping to dismantle unconscious biases that hinder inclusion.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Second, expanding outreach and facilitation for workplace integration.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Can there be staff to walk the ground in neighbourhood town centres to share about these programmes at the local level with merchants and small retail shops?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is easy to overlook the single trees when an imperative to be efficient prompts us to focus on bigger-scale wins of entire forests.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I ask that we do not skip over the small retailers who may turn out to be great allies in this effort, in favour of larger companies who may have bigger hiring capacity, but also require a bigger change-making effort to get the entire staff community aligned.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: There is a Malay saying: sikit-sikit, lama-lama jadi bukit.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Small results over time can create a big impact.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If everyday Singaporeans see PWSNs gainfully employed, actively contributing in the shops they frequent, in every neighbourhood, societal perception is sure to improve.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Even the families and caregivers' perception of their own children can improve.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can work towards the vision of Every Neighbourhood an Inclusive Neighbourhood and set a minimum target to enable X number of shops to be enabling employers in each locality for a start.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Facilitators play a crucial role in being a bridge to ensure that accessibility goes beyond infrastructure – it is also about attitudes, engagement and participation of both the employer and the employed.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I urge SG Enable to look into setting up satellite teams of facilitators within each Community Development Council that will help work with local merchants and propagate the success stories island-wide.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Chairman, a truly inclusive society does not merely accommodate persons with disabilities – it values, respects and celebrates them.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We must not stop at rhetoric but commit to real, structural change through investment, awareness, representation and support systems.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I urge this House to take decisive action to champion these expansion efforts for a fairer future for all who are differently abled.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Anyone, including their families, employers and the community, can make the top-ups to these eligible members' Special Accounts or Retirement Accounts.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I think this is a very good scheme and can I ask MSF to elaborate on the following.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: One, does the definition of disabilities include those with mental illnesses?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Two, why does it take almost one year for this new scheme to be implemented?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Can families and employers keen to start the top-up for persons with disabilities do so earlier this year instead?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: And lastly, what is the difference in policy rationale and impact of this new scheme compared to the services provided by the Special Needs Trust Company which is also supported by MSF?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng, you can take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: In particular, when they turn 18 years old, there is a significant shift in the institutional system as it is more fragmented and less supportive.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: One of the primary concerns for PwDs is employment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Employers may lack awareness or resources to make necessary accommodations.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There could be misconceptions about the capabilities of PwDs, which could act both ways, either unrealistic expectations or underemployment.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Furthermore, PwDs may not have had equal access to education and vocational training, and this limits their employment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Employment is not just about financial independence; it also contributes to a sense of purpose, social identity and community participation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Therefore, the lack of employment opportunities can have profound implications on the self-esteem and social integration of PwDs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: As PwDs age, their parents or primary caregivers are also ageing themselves.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Hence, they face increased physical and emotional strain.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There may be a lack of suitable and affordable caregiving options, which can lead to stress and burnout for caregivers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Many caregivers also have to balance their caregiving responsibilities with their own employment, leading to financial and emotional pressures.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: We have already come a long way through the various Enabling Masterplans and efforts from the Government, businesses, and our partners and the community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Singapore has a robust framework of support and services for vulnerable individuals and their families, including those in residential homes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Support for the vulnerable is multifaceted, comprising financial aid, social services, healthcare and community involvement.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Many in residential homes are there for the long term, especially those who are aged or with disabilities and have little family support.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There is a growing demand for these services and volunteers to help them, given that Singapore's ageing population is a fact.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: For those who in residential homes, they may not have family to visit them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: They rely on the warmth and support of the home caregivers and volunteers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There is a risk of the lack of social connections and cognitive engagements as a result of social isolation or not being able to participate in societal activities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: We need to not only enhance support for those residing in homes but help uplift them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There are many opportunities for the community and the Government to do more, to ensure a holistic approach towards care for those in residential homes, such as better service integration, improved coordination of services across agencies, expanded housing options and affordability, improved caregiving support and more accessible mental health services.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There needs to be continual review and enhancement of policies to address emerging needs of the vulnerable in Singapore, to ensure our support remains relevant and effective.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Can MSF share its plans on how can we better uplift those who are most vulnerable, especially those within residential homes?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: MSF has designated 2025 as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Professionals.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: This acknowledges and appreciates the significant contributions made by social service professionals.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: These individuals are at the forefront of supporting and empowering the more vulnerable groups in society, including children, the elderly, persons with disabilities and families in need.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The celebration aims to raise awareness of the critical role these professionals play in fostering a more inclusive and compassionate society.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: It is important to attract and retain a strong workforce in the social service sector to meet the growing needs of the community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: To this end, we need to continuously review existing initiatives and strategies to enhance the appeal of a career in social service and to ensure that professionals in the field are well-supported.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: These include investment in professional development and training, career prospects and progression, as well as well-being of social service professionals.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
