text: Additionally, we need public campaigns and outreach efforts to highlight and emphasise the appeal associated with social service work.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: By showcasing the impact and fulfilment derived from a career in social service, passionate individuals can then be attracted to join the sector and make a difference in the lives of others.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: So, what more will MSF do to ensure the social service sector remains a career of choice?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Social workers and child protection officers play an important role in protecting and supporting vulnerable individuals and families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Their work often involves navigating complex situations, advocating for the rights and needs of those they support, and providing a lifeline to those in crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: It is important that they are equipped with the necessary resources, training and support to effectively manage both the practical and emotional demands of their job.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: In this context, what measures are being taken to ensure social workers and child protection officers have the resources and training necessary to effectively carry out their duties and manage the emotional demands of their work?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: What plans does the Ministry have to better attract, retain and support social service professionals in order to meet the growing demands and adapt to the changing needs of our society?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: How does the Ministry plan to address the mental health and well-being of social workers, ensuring they receive adequate support to cope with the emotional demands of their roles?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: What initiatives are being introduced to provide ongoing professional development and career advancement opportunities for social workers?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: And finally, in what ways is the Ministry collaborating with educational institutions to prepare future social workers for the challenges they will face in the field?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: These are social trends that we are familiar with and there is much to learn from interventions carried out by other developed countries with longer history and development.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: However, I felt that with our unique history, our nation building philosophy that has seen us leapfrog from third world to the first world in one generation and our multiracial and multi-cultural society, it will be beneficial to delve deeper and consider social interventions and approaches that will work better for Singaporeans in our context and in the changing times ahead.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to first declare that I am self-employed as a transformation coach providing well-being related coaching services.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I rise today to highlight a matter of utmost importance, what my colleague, Mr Louis Ng, said as the burning bicycles.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Basically, ensuring a thriving and sustainable organisational culture within our social service agencies (SSAs).

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These agencies are the backbone of our society's care system, providing critical support to our most vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Yet, those who dedicate their lives to service often work under immense stress, leading to burnout, attrition and a decline in service quality.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This indicates that many SSA employees worry about being judged for not being resilient enough at work.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This fear prevents them from seeking the support they need, worsening workplace stress and attrition that creates a vicious cycle of overwork for the remaining staff and burn-out.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: If we are to build a compassionate and resilient social sector, we must invest in the well-being of the very individuals who provide care.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I propose three key measures to strengthen the organisational culture within SSAs.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These assessments will provide crucial insights into workplace morale, leadership effectiveness and employee well-being.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: By systematically evaluating organisational health, we can proactively address emerging issues before they escalate, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Second, I call for mandatory mental wellness training for broad leadership under the Centre for Non-Profit Leadership's training programmes or by the many local training enterprises that have sprouted in recent years to enable our collective well-being, such as Growthbeans and Calm Collective.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Board members must be equipped to recognise and prevent unhelpful management practices and advocate for policies to create psychologically safe environments that prioritise staff well-being.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: A leader who understands the toll of social work is better positioned to enact meaningful change that supports the management, employees and beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These professionals will serve as an independent support system, offering a listening ear, suggest healthy coping strategies and provide guidance toward necessary resources.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Many frontline workers struggle in silence, so having an accessible, trained facilitator can make the difference between retention and resignation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This is not just a moral imperative, it is a strategic investment.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: A healthy organisational culture ensures SSAs can deliver consistent, high-quality care to those who need it the most.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, let us stand in solidarity with our social service workers and affirm our commitment to their well-being.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, the social service sector has come a long way in the past few decades, maturing in professional standing and practices.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Many more dedicated individuals have joined the social services as demand has grown in all areas.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: New initiatives continue to be launched to meet the evolving needs as we work toward ensuring that no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our sector continues to be heavily reliant on the constant inflow of professional staff and allied health workers.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Many SSAs require a percentage of foreign staff to fill a variety of roles.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We are training more social workers in our institutes of higher learning in anticipation of current and future needs.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: With our new social compact, I hope many more Singaporeans will see the social service sector as one that will present opportunity for a fulfilling career.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In the past, salaries in the sector trailed behind jobs in most other industry groups.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: At the sectoral level, how might we keep pace with societal changes and evolve to continue to serve Singapore society well?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Chairman, SSAs, particularly, Family Service Centres, play a critical role in supporting vulnerable families and ensuring they receive the necessary assistance to achieve stability.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Strengthening the delivery of family services is essential in addressing complex and evolving needs within the community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: As challenges become more multifaceted, ensuring that services and programmes are well-coordinated, accessible and impactful is key to improving social outcomes.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Could MSF elaborate on how it plans to enhance service delivery within the social service sector?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Specifically, how will the Ministry ensure that vulnerable families, especially those with multiple and complex needs, receive more holistic, integrated and effective support?
